scope: App project-label CRUD writes: POST collection and PUT/PATCH/DELETE detail, including OPTIONS metadata and unsupported-method dispatch when the last Django writes leave these paths. API v1 writes and bulk import remain separate. Existing GET/HEAD behavior is preserved.
reuse_analysis: Extend internal/projectlabelreads domain with writes. Reuse Django session/CSRF/protocol boundary and durable Celery publisher.
shared_transport_evidence: Reuse production session, CORS, content negotiation, slash handling, request-size and conditional API audit boundary. Raw Django Allow is captured in the OPTIONS fixtures. The current production proxy sends OPTIONS to Django until every method on the path retires and expands its Allow header to the full resource set. Candidate replay must assert that production Allow value, explicitly normalize only Allow for source comparison, and separately compare baseline and candidate proxy responses. For renderer failures, capture and compare the raw HTML response body; an absent Allow header remains absent. For NaN renderer failures, capture and compare the raw HTML response body and preserve the absent Allow header. The source fixtures record renderer failure bodies as raw_text_body. Go uses the shared marked HTML500 boundary for renderer failures and typed JSON500 for ordinary handler errors; the OpenAPI response carries the x-plane-renderer-failure metadata extension.

shared_contract.permission_classes: ProjectBasePermission executes in DRF initial() before TimezoneMixin activates user_timezone. POST requires active workspace role 15/20. Other writes require active project admin, or active project membership plus active workspace admin. The method decorator repeats project authorization after create/PATCH/DELETE cache invalidation.
shared_contract.timezone: Invalid timezone raises ZoneInfoNotFoundError; BaseViewSet handles it as KeyError and returns 400 {error: The required key does not exist.}. Base permission failure wins with 403.
shared_contract.protocol_ownership: Routing inventory retains HEAD/OPTIONS companions on the existing GET entries because reads and writes use separate families on each path. The generated write service implements the two authored OPTIONS methods. Once all methods are Go active, the existing retired read route makes the complete path route to Go; protocol fixtures and production-proxy comparison prove this composed ownership.
shared_contract.audit_effect: X-Api-Key on any session write triggers shared API audit independently of endpoint success. The POST fixture records the shared effect with real RabbitMQ; this is not API-key authentication.
shared_contract.request_worker_boundary: Successful DELETE saves only the label and publishes one durable soft-delete task. Descendants and issue associations are worker-owned and verified by the separate real RabbitMQ success fixture. A distinct source-only HTTP test injects publisher failure and proves the 500 JSON response plus committed soft-delete/audit/cache state; the injected failure itself is not recorded as a durable task.

production_proxy.detail: GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS

allow_composition.proof: Source fixtures assert raw Django Allow. Go replay must assert the production-composed Allow header and explicitly normalize only this header for direct Django comparison. Independently compare baseline and candidate production-proxy responses while Caddy still routes OPTIONS to Django until every method retires; never substitute raw Django Allow for the proxy response.
allow_composition.proxy_header_policy: Caddy expands Allow only when the upstream response already contains Allow. Assert the production-composed Allow values for OPTIONS and ordinary JSON responses; preserve the absence of Allow for PATCH sort_order NaN (HTML 500). Do not synthesize or normalize a missing header.
allow_composition.conditional_normalization: Normalize only the observed Allow header for source-versus-Go comparison when present. Assert its absence for POST first-label NaN, PATCH NaN, and PUT NaN renderer failures; do not synthesize it. For these failures, compare raw_text_body as well as status, Content-Type, database state, and cache state.

transport_entry.import: Select four inventory operations and their three referenced schemas from full-server.openapi.json; omit environment-only servers metadata. Reverse import via loom import openapi, then adopt first-class session cookies, raw request streams, typed source errors, and source-complete result fields.
transport_entry.protocol: Two authored OPTIONS methods share RuntimeCORS preflight. Reuse common session-service boundary for slashless redirects, request size, session lifecycle, negotiation, audit and Django preflight response. Extend that boundary generically to delegate ordinary OPTIONS to authored methods and supply resource parameters to unsupported-method authorization; preserve existing notifications.
transport_entry.validation_order: Raw request stream preserves permission_classes before timezone before method authorization/body access. Typed path decoder behavior is adapted by existing shared Django URL compatibility.
transport_entry.renderer_failure: The source records persisted nonfinite writes followed by renderer HTTP 500 for POST with no existing labels, PATCH, and PUT; POST with existing labels overwrites incoming NaN with max sort_order + 10000 and returns 201. The Go operation contract uses typed JSON500 for ordinary API failures and the shared marked HTML500 compatibility boundary for source renderer failures. OpenAPI documents this with x-plane-renderer-failure metadata (text/html; charset=utf-8). This is shared transport behavior, not a route-specific designed HTML error.
